The Acknowledgements page states that some of the poems in this collection were previously published in "The Crisis, Verse Craft, Abbott's Monthly, American Poetry Anthology of 1927, Quill Poems of 1929, and The Parnassian."

No issues of The Crisis were ever renewed. Searching the Catalog of Copyright Entries between 1965 and 1958, inclusive, yielded no renewals of Verse Craft, Abbott's Monthly, or any individual poems by Davis. The latter three books—The American Poetry Anthology, Quill Poems of 1929, and The Parnassian: A Collection of Prose and Poetry by Sixteen Members of the Younger Generation—are in the public domain due to publication before 1931. In "Ad Astra Per Aspera: Frank Marshall Davis", John Edgar Tidwell locates previous publication of some poems in the Kansas State Collegian. However, all his examples date to before 1930.

The Sierra Madre News is the longest, continuous running newspaper in the City of Sierra Madre. It was published from October 1906 to June 1999. The newspaper was published by R. T. Cowles and yearly subscriptions cost $1.50. Successive editors include: C.W. Hill, George Morgridge, L.R. Goshorn. Clifford C. Ward, Peter Ward, Edgar W. Jenkinson, William F. Thomas, Ed E. Herwig, R. Robert Evans, Jannene G. Reed, and Michael De Wees. The paper was printed with a hand press, and then a two-revolution cylinder press, and starting in 1947 a 52-inch Miehle flat bed double revolution press, and finally using the offset method.
For additional information see <a href="https://californiarevealed.org/islandora/object/cavpp%3A147752" rel="nofollow">California Revealed</a>.
